title: grammar-priority-fallbacks-token-boundary-resolver-and-streaming-toolcall-framing
author: Priya Raman
description: Motivation: constrained-decoding backends (CFG + regex) have been brittle when tokenizers split grammar terminals across byte/word boundaries; this caused streaming truncation and malformed tool/function call frames observed in customer incidents (SUP-887). This PR introduces a priority-driven grammar fallback chain and a tokenizer-aware boundary resolver that normalizes constraint matching against tokenized streams. It also updates the OpenAI-compat function-calling framing to be more resilient to partial streaming boundaries. Design summary: 1) GrammarPriorityResolver: assigns priority to CFG nodes and exposes deterministic fallback semantics when a token boundary prevents a direct match. 2) TokenBoundaryResolver: canonicalizes token sequences into boundary-safe fragments and synthesizes soft-boundary tokens for constrained samplers to consider (without changing model inputs). 3) Streaming Frame Guard: when streaming function/tool outputs, we buffer up to N tokens (configurable, default 6) to confirm boundary integrity before emitting function-call start/stop events; falls back to chunked continuation if ambiguity remains. 4) OpenAI-compat shim: retains existing API surface but adjusts the streaming chunk framing wire format when constraints are active to avoid premature function call termination. Compatibility & risk: backward-compatible at API level; internal sampling path changes may affect deterministic outputs in corner cases — added canary tests and a staged rollout. Test plan: unit tests for CFG fallback permutations, tokenizer fixtures for 6 common tokenizers (BPE, SentencePiece variants), integration e2e that simulates a slow streaming client to validate frame guards, and perf regression benchmarks. Rollout: feature flag rollout by account tier (dev flag -> Canary -> 25% -> 100%) and metric monitoring for service-level latencies and malformed function-call rates. Related: ties to ENG-1423 (constraint stability) and ENG-1568 (streaming tool/frame resilience).

comments: Marco Gutierrez (reviewer): The grammar fallback approach looks sane; two questions — how do we guarantee termination on pathological CFGs, and can we bound memory on the resolver?
Author (Priya Raman): We limit fallback depth to 8 by default and add a circuit-breaker that converts to a permissive match if depth exceeded; added tests for intentionally ambiguous CFGs.
Elaine Zhou (reviewer): The streaming buffering could increase tail latency. Can we make boundaries adaptive based on downstream latency SLOs?
Author (Priya Raman): Added STREAM_GUARD_ADAPTIVE flag and heuristic: default horizon 6 tokens, reduces to 2 when p95 tail latency > SLA, documented in rollout notes.
Jonah Patel (approver): Verified unit + e2e on staging with BPE SentencePiece fixtures. Observed no measurable tokenization regressions. Approving to merge after addressing lint error in stream_shim.

merge_commit_message:
Grammar priority fallback + tokenizer boundary resolver; streaming frame guard; OpenAI-compat shim

Implements priority-driven grammar fallbacks and tokenizer-aware boundary resolution to stabilize constrained decoding and streaming function/tool call framing. Adds tests, telemetry, and canary rollout flags.
release_notes: Improves robustness of constrained decoding (CFG & regex) by handling tokenizer boundary splits and reducing malformed function/tool call frames during streaming. Adds a streaming frame guard to reduce premature tool-call termination. Rollout behind feature flag; no API changes.
notes_and_followups: Monitor telemetry: telemetry.events.constraint_mismatch_rate and telemetry.events.function_frame_resync_count for 2 weeks post-rollout.
Follow-up: port TokenBoundaryResolver to C++ core path for Dedicated performance (ENG-1689).
Follow-up: consider exposing STREAM_GUARD_HORIZON as per-route config for low-latency endpoints.
